A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same D-MPC work. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables and Appendices A–J are readable and support reliable comparison despite extensive reformatting.

before.justification: V1 reports original D4RL evaluations, novel-reward demonstrations, dynamics adaptation, component ablations, policy distillation and runtime measurements.

after.justification: V2 retains these original empirical results and adds a multi-step MLP ablation and a qualitative Diffuser comparison on novel rewards.

M1.justification: The diffusion action proposal, dynamics model, objective and planning procedure remain unchanged. SSR is renamed a sampling-based planner. Section 3.2 clarifies learning J consistently with the existing Appendix E.4; the new MLP variant is an experimental control.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same D4RL locomotion, Adroit and Kitchen tasks, dynamics-prediction datasets, Walker2D height objectives and simulated torque defect. The added comparisons use existing task coverage.

E2.justification: Section 4.2 newly reports evaluating Diffuser against D-MPC on novel-reward tasks, beyond its existing benchmark and dynamics-adaptation comparisons. Section 4.4.4 also introduces a comparator using multi-step MLPs for both action proposals and dynamics. Existing table comparator sets remain unchanged.

E3.justification: The new Section 4.4.4 experiment introduces a control with two-layer, 4096-hidden-unit multi-step MLPs using flattened sequence inputs. Previously reported metrics, training budgets, planning settings and adaptation procedures remain unchanged; no rerun or revised configuration of existing experiments is established.

E4.justification: V2 adds an expressiveness ablation replacing both multi-step diffusion components with multi-step MLPs. This supplements v1's comparisons of single-step versus multi-step models and diffusion versus MLP/ART dynamics by testing whether multi-step prediction alone suffices.

E5.justification: The 30-episode mean/standard-error reporting, Figure 2 percentile bands and runtime standard errors are retained. No new seed counts, uncertainty procedures or statistical tests are specified. The new Diffuser statement about no significant difference does not document a significance test.

E6.justification: Section 4.4.4 newly reports a normalized score of 50.01 for the multi-step MLP variant, compared with the retained D-MPC average of 65.98. Section 4.2 adds the qualitative finding of no significant performance difference from Diffuser on novel rewards. Existing numerical results in Tables 2–4 and 7 and Figures 1–2 are unchanged.

T1.justification: The MPC objective, probabilistic factorizations, diffusion formulation, state-normalization definitions and ART loss are retained. No theorem, proof, formal assumption or substantive mathematical derivation is added or revised.

C1.justification: The introduction drops proposing SSR as a separate contribution and instead emphasizes demonstrated reward and dynamics adaptation using a simple sampling-based planner. The central D-MPC, benchmark-performance and adaptation claims remain intact.

C2.justification: V2 replaces the sample-efficiency rationale with an argument about supervised dynamics prediction versus multimodal policy learning and credit assignment. It adds explanations connecting delayed consequences in D4RL to long-horizon planning and the MLP ablation to model expressiveness, and qualifies the advantage over Diffuser after reporting novel-reward parity.

D1.justification: V2 documents the new MLP control's depth, width and flattened inputs. Section 4.1 also newly states intended approximate compute parity with Diffuser. This is additional documentation, not evidence of changed existing architectures; Appendix E's specifications and the hardware, training and planning details are retained.

R1.justification: V2 adds Policy-Guided Diffusion, Model-based Diffusion, DyDiff and Zhu et al.'s representation-complexity work. It distinguishes known-dynamics trajectory optimization and synthetic-data generation from D-MPC's learned-model planning. The broader research positioning is preserved.

P1.justification: V2 replaces SSR terminology throughout, revises the contribution list and J-learning explanation, and expands several motivation and discussion passages. Section 4.4.4 is added, but the overall narrative order and appendix organization remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: The document switches throughout from the DeepMind template to TMLR formatting, substantially changing the author/abstract layout, typography, page geometry, headers, footers and placement or sizing of displays. Existing figures are retained, while Table 1 adds PGD; the major change is the document-wide presentation.

improvement.justification: The new multi-step MLP control supplies useful evidence about the contribution of diffusion beyond multi-step prediction. The Diffuser reward comparison, clearer J-learning description and expanded related work improve interpretation and positioning. These are limited gains: the core evidence remains unchanged, and the new comparisons provide only an aggregate score or qualitative finding without additional uncertainty details.
